mcq.why: The only non-zero entries are on the diagonal and 4 ≠ −12, so it is a diagonal matrix; a scalar matrix would need equal diagonal entries.
For A = [a b; c d] the adjoint is [d −b; −c a], so adj A = [1 2; −3 −1].
The matrix is not invertible when its determinant is 0: 5d − 2(1.5) = 5d − 3 = 0, so d = 0.6.
The determinant of [1 2; 0 1] is 1, so its inverse is [1 −2; 0 1].
√x = −10 has no solution: a square root is never negative (squaring gives x = 100, which does not satisfy it). The solution set is empty.
√(5x + 3) = 2 gives 5x + 3 = 4, so x = 1/5, and it checks.
|5x/3| = 5 gives x = 3 or x = −3. Option a is the closest: it prints only {3}, but the solution set is {3, −3}.
|−x| = 0 only when x = 0, so the solution set is {0}.
(5, −2): x positive and y negative is the fourth quadrant.
(−3, 8): x negative and y positive is the second quadrant.
(−6, −6): both negative is the third quadrant.
x = a is a vertical line, which is parallel to the y-axis.
The diagonals of a square are perpendicular (they are also congruent, option c); they are never parallel.

Options a, b and c are all true for an equilateral triangle (its perpendicular bisectors are congruent, concurrent and also its angle bisectors); d is false, since perpendicular bisectors of a triangle meet at a point.
Parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels are equal in area; they need not be congruent or similar.
